newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa believes Zaire rebels serious about peace.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa believes Zaire rebels serious about peace.

text.p: South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Thursday he believed Zairean rebels were serious about peace and democracy.
Delegations representing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces have seized a quarter of Zaire since October, are due to meet in South Africa this weekend.

Pahad told state radio that South Africa had gained the impression from Kabila, who held preparatory discussions in Pretoria last month, that he was committed to democracy in the Central African country.
"We've always had the feeling from the first proximity talks in South Africa that the rebels were committed to finding a peaceful solution.

"They wanted to be sure the negotiations would not take place over a protracted period...and ultimately they wanted to be sure that any negotiations must have as an objective finding the process that will lead to genuine democracy," Pahad said.
He said the situation in Zaire demanded that a political solution be found as soon as possible.
"I would hope that while a ceasefire will be an element (in the talks), they will use the opportunity to discuss the modalites for any future, more detailed negotiations," he said.
"A ceasefire must be the first step to finding a possible long-term political solution."
The team due to represent Mobutu's government was expected to meet in Zaire on Thursday to harmonise views on the agenda of the talks and leave for Pretoria on Friday.
The team, headed by Mobutu's security adviser Honore Ngbanda, includes opposition representatives and supporters of Mobutu, who has ruled the country since seizing power in 1965.
The rebels, who have vowed to topple Mobutu, want the talks to lead to a meeting between him and Kabila.
